title: incident-bot: autodiagnostics runbook prioritization and escalation context
author: Diego Ramos
description: Motivation: improve the quality and operational usefulness of runbook suggestions produced by incident-bot autodiagnostics. Prior work surfaced relevant runbooks but lacked clear prioritization and escalation context which made on-call decisions slower. This PR introduces a priority scoring model for runbook suggestions, attaches escalation context (recent paged owners, last action timestamps, SLA/SLO impact summary), and surfaces rationale telemetry so SREs can understand why a suggestion was recommended. Changes are backward compatible with existing message schemas and opt in via a feature flag. What this PR does: 1) Adds a runbook scoring pipeline that weights SLO impact, historical success rate, and recent signal match; 2) Augments runbook metadata with escalation_context fields (paged_teams, last_pager_timestamp, recent_changes_link, estimated_slo_impact); 3) Emits structured telemetry events for suggestion ranking (for later analysis in SLO toolkit dashboards); 4) Adds on-call helper shortcuts to the bot message (quick-ack, runbook-open, create-incident) and idempotent handlers; 5) Adds unit and e2e tests, and updates docs and Linear tickets. Migration and rollout: feature flag `autodiag_prioritization_v1` defaults to off. We will enable for internal SRE alpha, run telemetry for 48 hours, validate quality metrics, then progressively roll out to all teams. Checklist: [x] tests added, [x] docs updated, [x] telemetry hooked, [x] feature-flag gate, [x] reviewers approved. Related: ENG-2890 implements prioritization heuristics, ENG-2984 ties suggestions to SLO toolkit scoring. Breaking changes: none.
